svg.title: The six compression techniques compared by token reduction and retention
svg.desc: A hand-drawn table of six compression techniques. Each row names the operation, shows its token-reduction range as a floating bar on a shared nought-to-a-hundred scale, and states what survives. Windowing drops everything older than N turns for fifty to ninety per cent reduction, with bimodal retention: everything inside the window, nothing outside. Summarisation replaces a span with an LLM summary for eighty to ninety-five per cent, retaining seventy to ninety-five with a careful prompt and forty to sixty with a careless one. Tool-result clearing keeps the conclusion and drops the body for seventy to ninety-five per cent at effectively full retention, because the result is re-callable. Priority pruning trims the lowest class first for twenty to sixty per cent. Semantic chunking groups by topic for eighty to ninety-five per cent at the highest retention of the lossy techniques. Prompt-level compression reports several-fold to twentyfold on its own benchmarks, flagged as an upper bound needing local measurement.
svg.text: Six ways to compress, and what each one costs
Token reduction is the easy half. What survives it is the half that decides whether the next turn works.
Drop everything older than N turns.
Replace a span with an LLM summary.
Keep the conclusion, drop the body.
Default to priority pruning plus tool-result clearing: cheap, predictable, composable, and both keep everything they do not drop.
